tool_input.commit_message:
Mission-close state for cluster 3, written by `ethos mission result` and
`ethos mission close` after PR #515 merged as 6f61406. Tracked
deliberately per DES-058's two-zone split: sealed chunks are
git-tracked, the live tail stays gitignored.

Contents: the round-1 result artifact (verdict pass, files_changed
counts taken from git diff --numstat rather than written by hand), the
updated contract and delegation record, and the sealed session log.

Review found one real defect, in the artifact itself. The PR-merge
evidence entry had been written unquoted:

    - name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — 6/6 CI checks green, ...

YAML treats an unquoted ` #` as a start-of-comment, so everything from
`#515` onward was discarded at parse time, leaving `name: PR` with
`status: pass` intact. `ethos mission result` accepted it and it
round-tripped through close without a warning — a record asserting
success about something it no longer described, which is the same
defect class cluster 3 existed to eliminate, one level up in the record
of the fix. Hand-corrected here because results are append-only and the
mission is closed, so no CLI correction path exists. The other eight
evidence names were checked and parse intact. Filed as ethos-i1z8.

One finding rejected: audit entries in session 00063978 were flagged
for omitting delegation_id d-2026-09-10-001. That session is a bare
Agent spawn for a review-fix round, never a delegation, so the absence
is correct — tagging it would assert work happened under a contract
that never governed it. The entries are also sealed chunks, so editing
them would break their seal regardless.

tool_input.description: Fix repomiss tests and YAML truncation
tool_input.name: bwk-cleanup
tool_input.prompt:
Two small, independent fixes on branch `fix/repomiss-tests-and-evidence-truncation` in <repo>. Both are already diagnosed — do not re-investigate from scratch, but do verify each premise before acting. Do NOT push; commit and report, the leader pushes.

## Fix 1 — `internal/repomiss` has no tests at all

`internal/repomiss/repomiss.go` is 97 lines and has zero test files, so it produces no `ok` line in `make check` and reports 0.0% coverage. It is a dependency-free leaf type shared by the four layered stores (which produce misses), plus `internal/vendor` and `internal/doctor` (which verify completeness) — so it is exactly the kind of package where a silent regression propagates widely.

Surface to cover:
- `MissingRef.String()` — renders `{kind}/{slug}`.
- `ErrIncompleteRepoSet.Error()` — aggregates every miss, names each `Path`, and advises `ethos vendor <handle> --apply`. The `--apply` is load-bearing per its own comment (bare `vendor` only plans), so pin that it is present.
- `New(handle, missing)` — returns nil on empty, otherwise an `*ErrIncompleteRepoSet` with `Missing` already sorted.
- `Sorted(refs)` — orders by kind then slug, and **returns a copy**. Pin that the input slice is not mutated; that is the property most likely to be broken by a future "optimization" and it is invisible without a test.

Cover happy path, empty input, single vs multiple misses, and stable ordering across differing input orders (the doc comment says an unstable diagnostic is unusable in CI — prove it is stable). Also verify `errors.As` recovers `*ErrIncompleteRepoSet` from `New`'s `error` return, since callers depend on that.

Test the exported behaviour, not the implementation. Do not change `repomiss.go` unless you find an actual defect — if you do, report it separately rather than folding it in silently.

## Fix 2 — `ethos mission result` silently accepts YAML-comment-truncated evidence names

Verified, and it bit us for real on PR #516. A result file contained:

```yaml
- name: PR #515 merged as 6f61406 — 6/6 CI checks green, 17 review threads resolved
  status: pass
```

YAML treats an unquoted ` #` as a start-of-comment, so the parsed name was just `PR`. Validation at `internal/mission/result.go:217-221` only requires a non-empty name, and `"PR"` is non-empty — so it passed, was written to `results.yaml`, and round-tripped through `ethos mission close` with `status: pass` intact. A record asserting success about something it no longer described.

Implement a real check, not a length heuristic. At load time you have both the raw file bytes and the parsed struct: detect when a scalar value was truncated by an unquoted `#`. Concretely — for each evidence entry, find its raw source line and determine whether the text after `name:` contains an unquoted ` #` that YAML discarded. When it did, reject with an error naming the entry index, showing the parsed value versus the raw line, and telling the user to quote the value. An arbitrary minimum length would reject legitimate short names and miss long truncations; do not do that.

Consider whether the same trap applies to other free-text scalars in the result schema (`author`, `prose`, `open_questions` entries) and cover them if the mechanism is identical — fix the class, not the instance. Use judgement on `prose` if it is a block scalar, where `#` is literal and must NOT be flagged; if so, say that explicitly in your report.

Also update the `--help` examples in the `mission result` command so evidence names are quoted, since the current unquoted examples actively invite this for any name citing a bead ID or PR number — the most natural things to cite.

Confirm this fix red before it lands: a test with the exact `- name: PR #515 merged as ...` line that fails (submission accepted) pre-fix and passes (submission rejected) post-fix. Paste the pre-fix output.

## Gates

`make check` green with race. Report BOTH the `ok` count and the `FAIL` count — a zero FAIL alone cannot distinguish nothing-failed from nothing-ran. Pipe through `tee`, never redirect. No suppressions.

`internal/repomiss` must now produce an `ok` line with non-zero coverage — state the number.

Do not touch `tests/behavioral`: its 0.0% is correct, everything there is behind `//go:build behavioral` and needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` plus the `claude` CLI. I already verified that; it is not a defect.

Commit the two fixes separately. Report what you did and anything you rejected with evidence.

---
name: feedback-fix-dont-file
description: Fix small issues immediately instead of filing follow-up beads; closing one bead while opening three is the anti-pattern
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

When I find a small problem mid-task, I fix it in the current change. I do
not file a bead and move on. Jim's words: "you close one bead and open
three" and "being a deferral bead factory. Super annoying behavior."

**Why:** CLAUDE.md already says this and I was inverting it — "If you see a
problem — in code you wrote, code a reviewer flagged, or code you happen to
be reading — you fix it. Do not classify issues as 'existing' to justify
ignoring them." Plus "Default to T4 when in doubt," and T4 work has no bead:
the commit is the record. A bead for a 30-minute fix costs more to file,
triage, and re-load context on later than the fix does now. It also inflates
the backlog, which makes the backlog less useful as a signal.

**How to apply:** Default to fixing it in the branch I already have open. File
a bead only when the work genuinely cannot ride along — a different repo, a
design decision needing the operator, or a change large enough to warrant its
own review cycle. Before filing, ask "could I just do this now?" and if the
answer is yes, do it. Also verify the premise before filing: I filed a P1 for
Windows CI when Windows is not a supported platform, and half of another bead
was a misread of a `//go:build` tag. See [[feedback-strict-definition-of-done]]
and [[feedback-coo-owns-backlog]].
